result.note: A thin weekly roundup. Tested the grid stress and its causes, the USD 20 billion transmission approval and the US tariff exemption for specialty medicines.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about the stress on India's power grid in the week to 3 October 2026:
items: Weak monsoon rains boosted hydropower output and eased pressure on coal-fired generation.
The Centre ordered factory-owned coal plants to run flat out to help keep the grid afloat.
Coal stocks had fallen to about a week of supply.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 1 is wrong because the story says weak monsoon rains sapped hydropower rather than boosting it. With coal stocks down to a week of supply, the Centre had to call on factory-owned coal plants to support the grid.
questions.source: Weak monsoon rains sapped hydropower, and coal stocks were down to just a week of supply.

questions.prompt: In the week to 3 October 2026, the Government of India approved USD 20 billion for which of the following?
options: Transmission lines for long-term solar ambitions
Pumped hydro storage projects in the Himalayas
A fleet of new nuclear power reactors
questions.explain: The USD 20 billion is meant to build the transmission lines India needs for its long-term solar plans. The approval came in the same week that a near power crunch showed how fragile the grid remains.
questions.source: even as the government approves USD 20 billion to build the transmission lines needed for its long-term solar ambitions

questions.prompt: In the week to 3 October 2026, India secured a key tariff exemption from the United States for which category of its exports?
questions.explain: India won the tariff exemption for its specialty medicines. Even so, trade friction and diplomatic disagreements over regional policy with Washington remain unresolved.
questions.source: India secured a key tariff exemption for its specialty medicines, but trade friction and diplomatic disagreements over regional policy remain very much on the table.
